[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Metrics in Performance Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Performance testing is not merely about generating load; it is about measuring the right signals to evaluate system reliability, speed, and scalability. To do this effectively, engineers rely on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and system metrics."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Core Performance Metrics"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Core metrics form the foundation of any performance test report. They provide raw data regarding how the application and infrastructure behave under stress."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Response Time: The total time it takes for the system to receive a request and return a response."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Throughput: The number of transactions, requests, or megabytes processed by the system within a specific time unit (e.g., Transactions Per Second - TPS)."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Error Rate: The percentage of failed requests relative to the total number of requests sent during the test."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Understanding Percentiles"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Average response time can often be misleading because outliers skew the data. Performance testers rely heavily on percentiles (such as the 90th, 95th, or 99th percentiles) to understand the true user experience."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"90th Percentile (p90): 90 percent of all requests were completed faster than this value, while 10 percent took longer."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"95th Percentile (p95): Often used as a standard SLA benchmark to filter out intermittent network spikes."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Resource Utilization Metrics"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"While client-side metrics show how the user experiences the system, resource utilization metrics explain why the system behaves the way it does."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"CPU Utilization: The percentage of processing capacity being used by the server."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Memory Usage: The amount of RAM actively consumed by the application and operating system."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Network I/O: The rate at which data is read from and written to the network interface."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Disk I/O: The input/output operations per second (IOPS) on the storage subsystem."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Defining Clear SLAs and SLOs"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before executing any script, you must define Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs) based on business requirements."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"Example SLA Definition:
- Peak Load: 500 Concurrent Users (Virtual Users)
- Throughput Target: Minimum 250 TPS
- Response Time: 95th Percentile under 1.5 seconds
- Error Rate: Less than 0.5% under full load"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering performance KPIs allows engineers to pinpoint bottlenecks accurately, prevent production outages, and ensure applications scale efficiently under heavy user traffic."}]
